title: Meizuno — Overview
description: Stack health, uptime, host, and error logs up front; Traefik, the databases and monitoring's own footprint in collapsed rows. Provisioned from git — edit grafana/dashboards/meizuno-overview.json, because the file overrides UI changes on reload.

panels.title: Units and how to read this

options.content:
## Units on this dashboard

| On screen | Unit | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| `%` | percent | Share of a capacity: CPU across all 6 cores, RAM of total, connections of `max_connections`, 5xx of all requests. |
| `B` `KiB` `MiB` `GiB` | bytes, **binary** | 1 KiB = 1024 B, 1 MiB = 1024 KiB. Grafana shows IEC units, so `111.9 MiB` is ~117 MB in decimal marketing units. |
| `B/s` | bytes per second | Throughput — disk and network. |
| `req/s` | requests per second | Traefik, averaged over 5 minutes. |
| `s` `ms` | seconds | Request latency. |
| `CPU s/s` | CPU-seconds per second | `1.0` means one core fully busy for the whole interval. |
| plain number | count | Targets down, log lines, connections, Redis keys, active series. |

## How to read it

**Percentiles.** `p95 = 0.4 s` means 95% of requests finished faster than 0.4 s and 5% took longer. `p50` is the median. Watch p95 and p99 rather than an average — an average hides the slow tail, which is exactly the part users notice.

**Rates are 5-minute averages** (`rate(...[5m])`). A short spike therefore looks smaller than it was and takes a few minutes to appear at full height. For anything sharper, narrow the time range.

**Log levels** come from Loki's `detected_level`, assigned heuristically at ingest. It is dependable for plain-text logs (Go slog, uvicorn) but misses some lines from **forma** and **english**, which emit structured JSON — for those, query `| json | level =~ "warn|error"` instead of relying on the level filter.

**Empty panels are not always broken.** `5xx share` divides by total requests, so it is blank at zero traffic; latency percentiles need a few requests to exist; `Redis hit rate` stays blank until something reads from Redis.

**`Disk free — /`** reads the root filesystem explicitly. If it shows *No data*, node-exporter is not labelling the root mount as `/` — check *Free space per filesystem* below for the actual mountpoint names.

panels.title: Targets down (count)
panels.description: Scrape targets not answering. Should be 0 — anything else means an exporter or a service is down.

panels.title: Errors — last 1h (count)
panels.description: Across every container in the stack. Caveat: detected_level is a heuristic and misses some lines from forma and english, which log structured JSON — for those, filter with | json | level instead.

panels.title: Monitors now

targets.queryText:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT m.active AS active,
         (SELECT h.status FROM heartbeat h WHERE h.monitor_id = m.id ORDER BY h.time DESC LIMIT 1) AS status
  FROM monitor m
  WHERE m.type != 'group'
)
SELECT
  coalesce(sum(active = 1 AND status IN (1, 2)), 0) AS "Up",
  coalesce(sum(active = 1 AND status = 0), 0) AS "Down",
  coalesce(sum(active = 1 AND status = 3), 0) AS "Maintenance",
  coalesce(sum(active = 1 AND status IS NULL), 0) AS "Unknown",
  coalesce(sum(active = 0), 0) AS "Pause"
FROM latest
targets.rawQueryText:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT m.active AS active,
         (SELECT h.status FROM heartbeat h WHERE h.monitor_id = m.id ORDER BY h.time DESC LIMIT 1) AS status
  FROM monitor m
  WHERE m.type != 'group'
)
SELECT
  coalesce(sum(active = 1 AND status IN (1, 2)), 0) AS "Up",
  coalesce(sum(active = 1 AND status = 0), 0) AS "Down",
  coalesce(sum(active = 1 AND status = 3), 0) AS "Maintenance",
  coalesce(sum(active = 1 AND status IS NULL), 0) AS "Unknown",
  coalesce(sum(active = 0), 0) AS "Pause"
FROM latest

panels.description: Kuma's Quick Stats, read from Kuma's own database: each monitor by the status of its latest heartbeat. Pending counts as up, as it does in Kuma. Pause is a monitor switched off; Unknown is one with no heartbeat yet.

panels.title: Uptime events

targets.queryText:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', h.time) AS "DateTime", m.name AS "Name", h.status AS "Status", h.msg AS "Message"
FROM monitor m
JOIN heartbeat h ON h.monitor_id = m.id AND h.important = 1
WHERE h.time >= datetime($__from / 1000, 'unixepoch') AND h.time <= datetime($__to / 1000, 'unixepoch')
ORDER BY h.time DESC
LIMIT 500
targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', h.time) AS "DateTime", m.name AS "Name", h.status AS "Status", h.msg AS "Message"
FROM monitor m
JOIN heartbeat h ON h.monitor_id = m.id AND h.important = 1
WHERE h.time >= datetime($__from / 1000, 'unixepoch') AND h.time <= datetime($__to / 1000, 'unixepoch')
ORDER BY h.time DESC
LIMIT 500

panels.description: Every time a monitor changed status in the selected range, newest first, with Kuma's message — the list on Kuma's dashboard. A backup that failed verification says why since the backup script started sending a reason.

panels.title: RAM (%)
panels.description: Derived from MemAvailable, so page cache does not count as used.

panels.title: Disk free — / (GiB)
panels.description: Free space on the ROOT filesystem. An earlier version took min() across all filesystems and ended up reporting /boot/efi (a ~100 MiB vfat partition) instead — alarming and useless. If this reads No data, node-exporter is not labelling the root mount as "/"; check the trend panel below for the real mountpoint names. This is the stack's nearest risk: Loki has no disk-space limiter of its own.

panels.title: Free space per filesystem (GiB)
panels.description: With alerting deferred, the slope of these lines is the only early warning there is. Small partitions such as /boot/efi show up here too — that is fine in a trend, it was only misleading as a headline number.

panels.title: CPU by mode (%)
panels.description: idle is excluded on purpose — the question is WHAT the CPU is busy with. Rising iowait points at the disk; steal means a noisy neighbour on the hypervisor.

panels.title: Load average (runnable procs)
panels.description: Average number of processes runnable or waiting on I/O. Compare against core count — 6 on this host. Sustained load1 above 6 means a queue.

panels.title: 5xx share (%)
panels.description: Blank at zero traffic: the denominator is zero, not a fault.

panels.title: Postgres connections (% of max)
panels.description: Open backends as a share of max_connections (100 here).

panels.title: Redis memory (MiB)
panels.description: maxmemory is 384 MB with policy noeviction: at the ceiling Redis starts REFUSING writes rather than evicting keys.

panels.title: Query time per database (% of one core)
panels.description: CPU-seconds burned per second of wall clock, per database, shown as a share of ONE core: 50% means half a core busy on queries. To reach the individual query, use Explore with topk by queryid.

panels.title: VictoriaMetrics on disk (GiB)
panels.description: Retention is 15 days. If this climbs, check active series next to it — cardinality is usually the cause.

panels.title: Active series (count)
panels.description: Distinct time series seen this hour. The main driver is pg_stat_statements: every unique queryid adds its own series, capped at 5000 statements.

panels.title: Logs ingested — last 1h (MiB)
panels.description: Computed from the logs themselves, because Loki 3.6.1 does not expose loki_distributor_bytes_received_total. Retention is 7 days, so multiply by 168 for a rough steady-state disk estimate.
